--- title: Spline Smooths author: - name: Benjamin Vincent description: "Fit a 1-D smooth with ps() on a non-unit dose scale, then extrapolate with frozen knots." tags: - Basis Functions - Splines - Nonparametric image: thumbnails/splines.png jupyter: pathmc bread-crumbs: false --- A dose–response curve can bend without repeating and without needing a Gaussian-process lengthscale. `ps(dose, df=6)` is a cubic B-spline with a random-walk penalty on adjacent coefficients. The knots are frozen from the training doses, so `predict()` and `do()` replay that basis instead of refitting it. For the kernel alternative, see the [HSGP example](hsgp_1d.qmd). The [basis-terms guide](/user-guide/basis-terms.html) states when `bs()`, `ns()`, and `ps()` differ. ## Simulated dose–response The planted mean is a sine wave on doses 10 to 40. That range is deliberately not a unit interval: the default penalty is calibrated so its median effective degrees of freedom stay between a line and the full basis on a scale like this one. Observation noise has standard deviation 0.08. ::: {#cell-fig-spline-simulated .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code code-fold="true"} import warnings import arviz as az import matplotlib.pyplot as plt import numpy as np import pandas as pd import pathmc from pathmc.basis import get_basis from pathmc.parse import BasisCall FIG_WIDTH = 8 FIG_HEIGHT = 3.6 COLOR_OBSERVED = "#4c78a8" COLOR_POSTERIOR = "#f58518" COLOR_FUTURE = "#54a24b" COLOR_TRUE = "black" COLOR_NS = "#4c78a8" COLOR_BS = "#e45756" def response_mean(x): """One bend on a non-unit dose scale, in response units.""" return 1.5 + 0.8 * np.sin((x - 10.0) / 4.0) rng = np.random.default_rng(1) dose = np.linspace(10.0, 40.0, 60) df = pd.DataFrame({ "dose": dose, "response": response_mean(dose) + rng.normal(0.0, 0.08, size=dose.size), }) fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(FIG_WIDTH, FIG_HEIGHT)) ax.scatter( df["dose"], df["response"], s=16, alpha=0.55, color=COLOR_OBSERVED, label="Observed", ) ax.plot(dose, response_mean(dose), color=COLOR_TRUE, ls="--", lw=1.5, label="Planted mean") ax.set(xlabel="Dose (arbitrary units)", ylabel="Response (arbitrary units)") ax.legend() plt.show() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ![Simulated dose–response. Points include Gaussian observation noise; the dashed curve is the planted mean.](splines_files/figure-html/fig-spline-simulated-output-1.png){#fig-spline-simulated width=673 height=327} ::: ::: ## The model `ps()` is a standalone term. `df` is the number of free coefficients, not the number of interior knots. The smooth owns `beta_ps_response_dose` and the innovation scale `tau_ps_response_dose`, so it does not take a coefficient prefix. ::: {#e272ab28 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} model = pathmc.model("response ~ ps(dose, df=6)", data=df) model.equations() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display .cell-output-markdown execution_count=2} $$ \begin{aligned} \beta_{response} &\sim \text{Normal}(mu=0,\, sigma=10) \\ \sigma_{response} &\sim \text{HalfNormal}(sigma=1) \\ \beta_{ps,response,dose} &\sim \text{Normal}(mu=0,\, sigma=[10. 10. 1. 1. 1. 1.]) \\ \tau_{ps,response,dose} &\sim \text{HalfNormal}(sigma=2.0) \\[6pt] \mu_{response} &= \beta_{0,\,response} + \operatorname{ps}(\mathrm{dose}) \\ \mathrm{response} &\sim \text{Normal}(\mu_{response},\, \sigma_{response}) \end{aligned} $$ ::: ::: The coefficient prior is not one shared standard deviation. The first two coefficients, the unpenalized level and slope, keep `sigma=10`. The remaining coefficients are scaled by `tau`, whose default prior is `HalfNormal(sigma=2)`. ::: {#9137753c .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} model.priors() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display .cell-output-markdown execution_count=3} $$ \begin{aligned} \beta_{response} &\sim \text{Normal}(mu=0,\, sigma=10) \\ \sigma_{response} &\sim \text{HalfNormal}(sigma=1) \\ \beta_{ps,response,dose} &\sim \text{Normal}(mu=0,\, sigma=[10. 10. 1. 1. 1. 1.]) \\ \tau_{ps,response,dose} &\sim \text{HalfNormal}(sigma=2.0) \end{aligned} $$ ::: ::: ## Fit and recover the smooth `tau` and the penalized weights trade off, so the default target acceptance diverges. `target_accept=0.99` is the setting that samples this curve cleanly. ::: {#f651d48c .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} idata = model.fit(draws=800, tune=800, chains=4, random_seed=1, target_accept=0.99) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stderr} ``` NUTS[nutpie]: [beta_ps_response_dose, tau_ps_response_dose, beta_response, sigma_response] ``` ::: ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ```{=html} ``` ::: ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ```{=html} 

```
:::
:::


`mu_response` is the full linear predictor, intercept included.

::: {#cell-fig-spline-recovery .cell execution_count=5}
``` {.python .cell-code code-fold="true"}
mu = idata.posterior["mu_response"]
mu_draws = mu.stack(sample=("chain", "draw")).transpose("sample", ...).values
mu_mean = mu_draws.mean(axis=0)
mu_hdi = az.hdi(mu_draws, prob=0.94, axis=0)

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(FIG_WIDTH, FIG_HEIGHT))
ax.scatter(
    df["dose"],
    df["response"],
    s=16,
    alpha=0.45,
    color=COLOR_OBSERVED,
    label="Observed",
    zorder=1,
)
ax.fill_between(
    dose, mu_hdi[:, 0], mu_hdi[:, 1], color=COLOR_POSTERIOR, alpha=0.3, label="94% HDI", zorder=2
)
ax.plot(dose, mu_mean, color=COLOR_POSTERIOR, lw=2.5, label="Posterior mean", zorder=3)
ax.plot(
    dose, response_mean(dose), color=COLOR_TRUE, ls="--", lw=1.5, label="Planted mean", zorder=4
)
ax.set(xlabel="Dose (arbitrary units)", ylabel="Response (arbitrary units)")
ax.legend()
plt.show()
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display}
![In-sample posterior mean of the response with a 94% HDI. The dashed curve is the planted dose–response.](splines_files/figure-html/fig-spline-recovery-output-1.png){#fig-spline-recovery width=673 height=327}
:::
:::


The posterior mean follows the planted bend. That is the check that six penalized B-spline coefficients are enough for this curve.

## Extrapolate with the frozen knots

`do()` replaces the dose column and rebuilds the spline from the knots stored at fit time. The new grid has one value per observed row and sits past the last dose, so the call warns. The basis is still defined: `bs` and `ps` continue as a cubic polynomial, and `ns` would continue as a line.

::: {#3f8945f5 .cell execution_count=6}
``` {.python .cell-code}
future_dose = np.linspace(40.0, 48.0, len(df))
with warnings.catch_warnings(record=True) as caught:
    warnings.simplefilter("always")
    future = model.do(set={"dose": future_dose}, kind="predictive", random_seed=1)
print(next(item.message for item in caught if issubclass(item.category, UserWarning)))
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stderr}
```
Sampling: [response]
```
:::

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}
```
Intervention value [40.00, 48.00] for 'dose' is outside the observed data range [10.00, 40.00]. Results are extrapolations and should be interpreted with caution.
```
:::
:::


::: {#cell-fig-spline-extrapolation .cell execution_count=7}
``` {.python .cell-code code-fold="true"}
future_draws = future.dataset["response"].values.reshape(-1, future_dose.size)
future_mean = future_draws.mean(axis=0)
future_hdi = az.hdi(future_draws, prob=0.94, axis=0)

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(FIG_WIDTH, FIG_HEIGHT))
ax.scatter(
    df["dose"], df["response"], s=14, alpha=0.4, color=COLOR_OBSERVED, label="Observed", zorder=1
)
ax.fill_between(
    dose, mu_hdi[:, 0], mu_hdi[:, 1], color=COLOR_POSTERIOR, alpha=0.25, label="94% in-sample HDI"
)
ax.plot(dose, mu_mean, color=COLOR_POSTERIOR, lw=2.5, label="In-sample mean")
ax.fill_between(
    future_dose,
    future_hdi[:, 0],
    future_hdi[:, 1],
    color=COLOR_FUTURE,
    alpha=0.25,
    label="94% extrapolated predictive HDI",
)
ax.plot(future_dose, future_mean, color=COLOR_FUTURE, lw=2.5, ls="--", label="Extrapolated predictive mean")
extended = np.concatenate([dose, future_dose])
ax.plot(extended, response_mean(extended), color=COLOR_TRUE, ls="--", lw=1.5, label="Planted mean")
ax.axvline(40.0, color=COLOR_TRUE, ls="--", lw=1.2, label="Last observed dose")
ax.set(xlabel="Dose (arbitrary units)", ylabel="Response (arbitrary units)")
ax.legend(fontsize=8, ncol=2)
plt.show()
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display}
![In-sample posterior mean (orange) and extrapolated posterior predictive mean (green). The vertical line is the last observed dose. The dashed curve is the planted mean.](splines_files/figure-html/fig-spline-extrapolation-output-1.png){#fig-spline-extrapolation width=663 height=327}
:::
:::


The green band is an extrapolation, not a refit. Quantile knots from doses 40 to 48 would sit in a different place; `do()` does not recompute them.

Natural and B-spline tails are a property of the basis, visible without another sample. The curves below are least-squares fits of the planted mean, replayed on a grid that runs past the last dose.

::: {#cell-fig-spline-tails .cell execution_count=8}
``` {.python .cell-code code-fold="true"}
grid = np.linspace(10.0, 50.0, 200)
truth = response_mean(dose)


def _extended(name):
    basis = get_basis(name)
    call = BasisCall(name, "dose", {"df": 6})
    columns, state = basis.build_data(dose, call)
    beta, *_ = np.linalg.lstsq(columns, truth - truth.mean(), rcond=None)
    extended_columns, _ = basis.build_data(grid, call, state=state)
    return truth.mean() + extended_columns @ beta


fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(FIG_WIDTH, FIG_HEIGHT))
ax.plot(grid, response_mean(grid), color=COLOR_TRUE, ls="--", lw=1.5, label="Planted mean")
ax.plot(grid, _extended("ns"), color=COLOR_NS, lw=2.2, label="ns() least squares")
ax.plot(grid, _extended("bs"), color=COLOR_BS, lw=2.2, label="bs() least squares")
ax.axvline(40.0, color=COLOR_TRUE, ls="--", lw=1.2, label="Last observed dose")
ax.set(xlabel="Dose (arbitrary units)", ylabel="Response (arbitrary units)")
ax.legend()
plt.show()
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display}
![Least-squares spline fit of the planted mean, extended past the last dose. Natural-spline tails are linear; B-spline tails keep a cubic bend.](splines_files/figure-html/fig-spline-tails-output-1.png){#fig-spline-tails width=663 height=327}
:::
:::


Past the last dose the blue curve is a straight line and the red curve is not. Use `ns()` when an intervention beyond the observed range should not keep bending. Use `hsgp()` when the smooth should stop at a kernel boundary instead of extrapolating at all.

**Takeaway:** use `ps()` for a smooth penalty on a fixed B-spline, `bs()` for that basis without a penalty, and `ns()` when tails must be linear. Knots stay at the training quantiles under `predict()` and `do()`.
